questions.subject: Maths
questions.why: Subtract 3 from both sides: 5x = 25. Divide by 5: x = 5. Picking 25 means you stopped one step early — Thursday's test will love that trap.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Romeo and Juliet opens with a street brawl between servants of which two households?
questions.why: The two feuding houses — the brawl in Act 1 Scene 1 shows the hate is so old even the SERVANTS fight it.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which city was the great prize both sides fought over in the Crusades?
questions.why: Jerusalem — holy to Christians and Muslims both, which is exactly why it was worth centuries of war. This is your class topic this very week.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Which symbol means 'less than or equal to'?
questions.why: ≤ = less than OR equal to. Plain < has no 'or equal' — the little line underneath is the 'or equal' part. Fresh from Monday's lesson.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: The 14-line speech at the very start of R&J that tells the audience the whole story is called the…
questions.why: The Prologue — and sneaky bonus: its 14 lines make it a sonnet, a love poem, opening a play about a feud.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.why: Multiply both sides by 4: x = 24. Picking 1.5 means you divided again instead of undoing the division.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In the feudal system, peasants (serfs) worked the lord's land in return for…
options: Protection and a place to live
questions.answer: Protection and a place to live
questions.why: No wages, no ownership — labour in exchange for protection and tenancy. The bottom layer of the pyramid you taught back last week.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.why: Move the 2x left: 2x − 5 = 9. Add 5: 2x = 14. Divide: x = 7. X on both sides is exactly the Thursday-test level — this is the skill.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: You test whether the HEIGHT a ball is dropped from changes how high it bounces. The independent variable is…
questions.why: Independent = the thing YOU change on purpose (drop height). Dependent = what you MEASURE happening (bounce height). Controlled = kept the same (same ball, same floor). Same puzzle as last night, new costume — this one's worth locking forever.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Which value of x makes x + 3 > 10 true?
questions.why: You need x > 7. Try 7: that gives exactly 10, and 10 > 10 is FALSE — 'greater than' doesn't include equal. 8 gives 11 > 10 ✓. That edge is the whole point of inequality symbols.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: At the Capulet party (Act 1 Scene 5), why does Tybalt suddenly become furious?
options: He recognises Romeo — a Montague has crashed the party
Juliet refuses to dance with him
questions.answer: He recognises Romeo — a Montague has crashed the party
questions.why: Tybalt knows Romeo's voice. Capulet orders him to let it go — and that swallowed rage is the fuse for the duel later. Straight off this week's Scene 5 worksheet.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Your mate missed Monday's lesson and Thursday's test is coming. Explain to him: what are you actually DOING when you solve an equation like 4x − 5 = 2x + 9 — and what's the golden rule about the equals sign you must never break? Steps plus the rule, your own words.
